name: Random-modulator soundscape loop: resampled-chord drone with one random modulator on each voice's start position and pan, randomly shortened arp-driven drums, a randomly retimed delay with a +12 st pitch shifter and stepped grain size in its feedback, and a step-scanned vocal sampler
goal: Keep a slow (88 BPM) textural loop alive using random and step modulators rather than new notes. (1) Drone: resample a plucked chord into a sampler, set it up to sustain, and have one random modulator (no smoothing; slight clicks are accepted as character) move both sample start/playhead and pan, so each voice starts somewhere different and sits elsewhere in the stereo field. Run a delay in parallel with a convolution reverb. (2) Drums: half-note mallet/brush hits from an arpeggiator whose step count is randomly shortened (16 down to a minimum of 4 steps), so the loop never repeats the same way. Send it to a delay whose time in beats is randomly modulated with smoothing (about 1–8 beats), with a pitch shifter at +12 semitones inside the feedback and a step modulator on its grain size for metallic, sideways echoes. (3) Vocal: a vocal loop in a sampler driven by an 8-step transposing arp, a 16-step modulator choosing the playhead start each step, a band-pass with a slow LFO on frequency, random pan per note, a distortion macro stepped through 16 values, then delay with reverse blur. Delta vs our shimmer and granular skills: random/step modulation of sampler playheads and delay timing as the generative engine.

source.title: Deconstructing a Textural Soundscape | Creative Sprint #5 Breakdown
source.transcript_note: Loop breakdown; product presets and pack names omitted.

prerequisites: Sampler with modulatable sample start and pan; random and step modulators (Web Audio: AudioBufferSourceNode.start(when, offset) with a random offset per voice, implementation note)
Delay with modulatable time and an insertable pitch shifter in its feedback path

inputs.name: chord_resample
inputs.description: Rendered pluck/piano chord to turn into a drone

outputs.name: soundscape_loop
outputs.description: Evolving multi-layer textural loop that never repeats identically

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Leaving the playhead randomiser unsmoothed causes clicks. The presenter keeps them as character; smooth or crossfade if they're too loud.
Random delay-time modulation needs smoothing to avoid zipper jumps.
The pitch shifter in the feedback re-pitches every repeat (+12 cascades), so filter if it gets shrill.
Ranges quoted (16→4 steps, 1–8 beats, +12 st, 16 steps) are from the transcript; other amounts by ear.

steps.action: Resample a plucked chord into a sampler and set it up to sustain as a drone. Add one random modulator and map it to both sample playhead/start and pan.
steps.expect: Each new voice starts at a different point in the sample and lands at a different pan

steps.action: Process the drone through a standard delay in parallel with a convolution reverb.

Drums at slow tempo: half-note hits from a drum machine with two samples (mallet, brush) driven by an arpeggiator. Add a random modulator that shortens the arp length by up to −12 steps (16 down to 4).
steps.expect: Sparse percussion whose pattern never repeats the same way

steps.action: Send drums to a delay: random modulator with smoothing on delay time in beats (about 1 to 8), a pitch shifter at +12 semitones inside the feedback loop, and a step modulator on the shifter's grain size.
steps.expect: Metallic, octave-climbing echoes, especially in the sides

steps.action: Add a background drone layer (e.g. a pad preset with longer envelope/filter and chorus) playing the same chords lower, plus an optional texture drone into a big reverb with modulated warp, kept low in the mix.

Vocal layer: vocal loop in a sampler fed by an 8-step arp with transposition. Use a 16-step modulator to set a different playhead start per step, a slow LFO on a band-pass frequency, and a random modulator on pan.
steps.expect: Chopped, moving vocal fragments across the stereo field

steps.action: Vocal FX: distortion preset whose saturation macro is stepped through 16 values, then a delay with reverse blur.
steps.expect: Rhythmically varying grit and smeared echoes

verification: Repeated notes on the drone start from audibly different sample positions and pans.
The drum arp pattern length varies between 4 and 16 steps over successive bars.
Delay repeats climb in pitch by octaves inside the feedback.
Each vocal step begins at a different point of the loop.
